summary: This bill bars Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from owning or trading stocks, bonds, commodities, or other interests tied to defense contractors, requires divestment within 120 or 180 days (with civil fines up to $50,000 per violation), and allows tax-free sales of such assets.

scores.thoughts: The bill restricts personal stock ownership and trading by Members of Congress in defense contractors but does not alter any government spending levels, appropriations, or budgets. It is purely an ethics and divestment measure with no bearing on spending policy.

The bill includes a narrow tax-code amendment allowing nonrecognition of capital gains on required divestments. This is a highly targeted procedural relief rather than any broad change to tax rates or policy, so it has no meaningful impact on taxation.
No provisions relate to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions relate to firearms regulation or gun rights.
No provisions relate to immigration, borders, or related protections.
No provisions relate to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill targets financial interests in defense contractors but does not change defense spending levels, procurement policy, or military budgets. It addresses conflicts of interest only.
